# workflow-supervisor v0.3.0

Workflow Supervisor is now positioned as a portable verification and workflow-contract layer for Codex and Claude Code. It complements native models, skills, subagents, permissions, and hooks instead of trying to replace them with a larger prompt.

## Highlights

- Reduces the core supervisor from 608 lines to 162 lines and loads specialized guidance only when needed.
- Routes small tasks directly, bounded backlogs through a lean ledger, risky or ambiguous work through strict contracts, and planning requests without implementation.
- Makes all eight skills explicit opt-in so ordinary Codex and Claude Code work does not inherit supervisor overhead.
- Introduces strict `DossierV1`, raw worker-output, and normalized `WorkerReportV1` boundaries.
- Requires every final PASS to contain substantive evidence mapped to the dossier's acceptance rows.
- Uses role-specific Codex sandboxes and Claude Code permission modes, with verifier workers read-only.
- Strips credential-like environment variables by default and requires explicit dossier authority before forwarding them.
- Detects out-of-scope changes across dirty worktrees, ignored and untracked files, empty directories, nested repositories, Git control state, symlink escapes, and hard-link aliases.
- Makes install and uninstall manifest-owned, checksum-verified, transactional, overlap-safe, and rollback-safe while preserving unrelated target files.
- Rewrites the README around the project's defensible value: portable contracts, independent verification, resumability, and false-PASS prevention.

## Why This Release

New Codex and Claude Code models already provide strong planning, tool use, native subagents, and platform-specific permissions. The remaining reason to add Workflow Supervisor is not to make the model follow a longer prompt. It is to make delegated work bounded, independently checked, portable between supported agents, and harder to mark complete without evidence.

## Important Behavior

- Native Codex or Claude Code subagents remain the preferred transport when they can honor the required contract.
- The package CLI remains a one-shot portable delegation path, not a daemon or agent platform.
- The filesystem guard detects mutations but does not replace an operating-system sandbox.
- Publication, credentials, destructive actions, production changes, external messages, push, merge, and pull-request creation still require explicit authority.

## Validation

- `npm run validate`: 166 of 166 tests passed on the final versioned tree.
- The same 166-test suite passed on Node.js 18, 20, 22, and 25.
- Strict Draft 2020 schema compilation passed for all three schemas.
- Ruby Psych parsed the published DossierV1 YAML examples without YAML 1.1 boolean coercion.
- All 32 Markdown files passed the local-link audit.
- The 48-file `workflow-supervisor-0.3.0.tgz` passed validate, both CLI aliases, install, doctor, context emission, and uninstall as a consumer.

## npm Publication

This GitHub release prepares `workflow-supervisor@0.3.0`. npm publication is intentionally separate and will happen only after the GitHub release is verified.

```bash
npm publish
```
